flawed_step: 0010 | So I multiplied both halves by $g(n)$ obtaining $f(n) > M\cdot g(n)$
assessment_summary: Step 0010 is not justified because the proof never establishes that $g(n)>0$ eventually. Multiplying an inequality by a negative $g(n)$ reverses its direction. For example, $f(n)=-n$ and $g(n)=-1$ give $f(n)/g(n)=n\to\infty$, but multiplying $f(n)/g(n)>M$ by $g(n)=-1$ yields $f(n)<Mg(n)$, not $f(n)>Mg(n)$.
